https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/.body: epistat is a set of Rust crates for register-based epidemiology. Most estimators reproduce a function in R, and results are the same whatever the number of threads. The guides show the crates in use, and the source is on GitHub.

https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/fou.body:
Five small crates that the others build on. Each can be used on its own.
CrateWhat it does
epistat-rngSplitMix64 streams and bootstrap draws that reproduce across threads, platforms and languages.
epistat-statsSample quantiles, the normal distribution and floating-point sums that agree with R and Python to the bit.
epistat-linalgDense solves with fallbacks and row-blocked products on faer, with results that do not depend on the number of threads.
epistat-optimBFGS, Nelder-Mead, simplex methods, branch and bound and minimum-cost flow for small statistical problems.
epistat-testkitTest helpers for numerical code: tolerances, bit fingerprints, thread-count checks and R reference files.
Install any of them with cargo add, for example cargo add epistat-rng. Rust 1.85 or newer. Licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0.
https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/fou.description: Random number streams, quantiles and sums that agree with R, dense linear algebra, small optimisers and test helpers that the other crates build on.

https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/glm.body:
Generalised linear models fitted by IRLS as R’s glm.fit does, with results that do not depend on the number of threads.
Install
Rust 1.85 or newer. Licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0.
What it covers
Generalised linear models fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares, checked against R’s glm().
The multinomial logit, the model of the generalised propensity score.
The Gaussian and binomial elastic net, and the Park test of a variance function.
https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/glm.description: Generalised linear models fitted by IRLS as R's glm.fit does, with results that do not depend on the number of threads.

https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/inf.body:
Influence-function and sandwich variances, cluster-robust and bootstrap intervals that reproduce across thread counts.
Install
Rust 1.85 or newer. Licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0.
What it covers
Variances from an influence function, with or without clusters, and the sandwich covariance.
Multiplier and cluster bootstrap replicates, and confidence intervals from them.
Wald tests, simultaneous bands and Rubin’s rules for multiply imputed data.
https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/inf.description: Influence-function and sandwich variances, cluster-robust and bootstrap intervals that reproduce across thread counts.

https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/mat.body:
Matching for cohort studies: nearest-neighbour, optimal, full, subclass, exact, coarsened exact, genetic and cardinality matching, risk-set matching, propensity scores, balance and effect estimates, with results that do not depend on the number of threads.
Install
Rust 1.85 or newer. Licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0.
What it covers
The MatchIt methods: nearest-neighbour, optimal, full, subclass, exact, coarsened exact, genetic and cardinality matching.
Propensity scores, Mahalanobis and Euclidean distances, calipers and common support.
Risk-set matching in longitudinal cohorts, at the time a person becomes a case.
Balance statistics, matching weights, effect estimates and sensitivity analyses.

https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/mat.title: epistat-matching

https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/reg.body:
Calendar-year person-time, interval merging, connected components over shared keys and constant-price deflation for register data.
Install
Rust 1.85 or newer. Licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0.
What it covers
Day counts and civil dates, with the SAS epoch of 1960 beside the Unix epoch, and age under a named rule.
Merging of intervals that overlap or lie within a grace period, such as residence spells.
Connected components of rows that share a key, for example siblings through either parent.
ICD-10 codes, including the Danish register prefix, and their chapters.
Deflation to the prices of a reference year.

https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/seq.body:
Optimal-matching, Hamming and dynamic Hamming distances between state sequences, weighted k-medoids, silhouettes and null-model validation.

https://tkragholm.github.io/projects/sur.body:
Cox regression, Fine-Gray, Aalen-Johansen, multi-state occupation and the Titman-Putter test, with results that do not depend on the number of threads.
Install
Rust 1.85 or newer. Licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0.
What it covers
Kaplan-Meier and Nelson-Aalen curves, the log-rank test and restricted mean survival time.
Cox regression with ties, delayed entry, strata, weights, cluster-robust variance, residuals and the test of proportional hazards.
Competing risks: the Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence, the Fine-Gray model and absolute risks from cause-specific Cox models.
Multi-state models: occupation probabilities, Cox models per transition and the test of the Markov property.
Person-time tables, Lexis splitting and Poisson rate models, conditional logistic regression, standardisation and weighting.
Concordance, Brier score and time-dependent AUC.
